questions.question: What are Worker Threads in Node.js used for?
options: Running CPU-intensive tasks in parallel threads without blocking the event loop
questions.explanation: Worker Threads enable true parallelism for CPU-bound work while the main thread stays responsive.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Cluster module?
options: Creates child processes that share the same server port to utilize multiple CPU cores
questions.explanation: Cluster forks the process into workers (one per CPU core), all sharing the same port for load balancing.

questions.question: What is the performance issue?

questions.question: What is backpressure in Node.js streams?
options: When a writable stream can't keep up with a readable stream, signaling to slow down
Memory pressure from too many variables
questions.explanation: Backpressure occurs when data is produced faster than consumed. Streams handle this via the drain event and return value of write().

questions.question: What does libuv do in Node.js?
options: Provides the event loop, async I/O, thread pool, and cross-platform abstraction layer
questions.explanation: libuv is the C library that implements Node's event loop, file I/O, networking, and the default 4-thread pool.

questions.question: What is the V8 garbage collector's generational strategy?
options: Young generation (Scavenge) for short-lived objects + Old generation (Mark-Sweep-Compact) for long-lived ones
questions.explanation: V8 uses generational GC: fast Scavenge for new objects, slower Mark-Sweep-Compact for objects that survive multiple GC cycles.

questions.question: What is the security issue?

questions.question: What is the purpose of --max-old-space-size flag?
options: Sets the maximum heap memory for the V8 old generation in MB
questions.explanation: This V8 flag controls max heap memory. Default is ~1.5GB on 64-bit. Increase for memory-intensive applications.

questions.question: What is the difference between CommonJS (require) and ES Modules (import)?
options: CJS is synchronous and dynamic; ESM is asynchronous, statically analyzed, and supports tree-shaking
questions.explanation: ESM enables static analysis for tree-shaking and top-level await. CJS loads modules synchronously at runtime.
